REVIEW_DECISION: REJECT
RISK_CLASS: high-impact
SUMMARY: The prose contracts are sound: Factory owns mission, apply, gates and integration; profiles are adapters only; unknown telemetry is unavailable not zero; 200k/500k are warning/reflection, not cancellation; RCA permits harness_or_gate and requires counterfactual evidence before blaming a profile; trailers and receipts are harness-written; refactors are not forced onto Sol/Opus; the package stays proposed. Two enforcement holes in the pinned machine-readable layer contradict the declared properties. A model profile that simply omits `extends` is bound by no authority constraint at all in either the schema or the declared validator gate, and the high-impact dual-approval check can be satisfied by one review whose profile string contains both names. Both are fixable in this package.
FINDING: high | docs/factory-ng/schemas/factory.model-profile-v1.schema.json:1 and scripts/factory-ng-profile-validate.py:33 | Authority constraints are only enforced for `id == "staged-baseline"` (schema allOf clause 1) and for profiles that declare `extends` (schema allOf clause 2; validator `if not parent: continue`). A profile with neither passes both the schema and the declared gate while asserting `authority.model_edits_workspace: true` and `commit_push_deploy: true`. | Violates safety property 2 and property 1: the profile layer becomes able to broaden authority beyond the Ticket/baseline and take patch-application and deploy authority away from the harness, with the package's own deterministic gate reporting pass.
REQUIRED_CHANGE: (1) Require every non-baseline profile to declare `extends` (schema: `"required": ["schema","id","version","extends"]` unless `id == "staged-baseline"`), and in factory-ng-profile-validate.py replace `if not parent: continue` with a hard failure for any non-baseline profile lacking `extends`; add fixture `invalid-profile-no-extends-authority.json` (rogue authority, no `extends`) asserted as must-fail in scripts/test_factory_ng_contracts.py. (2) In factory.change-provenance-v1.schema.json, make high-impact approval provably independent: require at least two accepted reviews with distinct `review_sha256` and distinct `reviewer_profile`, and require exactly one to match the Sol pattern and one the Opus pattern (mutually exclusive, e.g. Opus branch adds `"reviewer_profile": {"not": {"pattern": "(^|[-_])sol([-_@]|$)"}}`); add fixture `invalid-provenance-high-impact-combined-reviewer.json` asserted as must-fail. (3) Move the `outcome == "accepted"` constraint from "every review accepted" to "at least one accepted review exists and no unresolved rejection", so an immutable record can retain an earlier `rejected` review instead of requiring its removal. (4) Hoist the baseline authority/budget assertions in factory-ng-profile-validate.py out of the per-child loop so they run even when no child profile is present.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: (a) Add docs/factory-ng/model-profiles/v1/qwen-autonomous.json = {"schema":"factory.model-profile/v1","id":"qwen-autonomous","version":"1.0.0","adapter":{"executable":"scripts/qwen-agentic-call.py"},"authority":{"model_edits_workspace":true,"harness_applies_patch":false,"harness_owns_tests_and_gates":false,"commit_push_deploy":true},"budget_policy":{"warning_is_hard_stop":true}} — Draft202012Validator accepts it (no `extends`, `id != "staged-baseline"`), factory-ng-profile-validate.py `continue`s past it, and scripts/test_factory_ng_contracts.py prints "factory-ng contract fixtures: pass"; a ticket routed to this profile lets the model edit and deploy directly. (b) Provenance record with contract_change_scope "high_impact" and reviews [{"decision":"accepted","reviewer_profile":"sol-opus-review@1","review_sha256":"sha256:one"}] validates: the single `contains` for Sol and the single `contains` for Opus are both matched by the same entry, so one review certifies a token-accounting-semantics change that requires independent Sol and Opus approval.
